n: After the chaos of Abimelech, Tola of Issachar rises to defend Israel. He is one of the “minor judges” whose stories are told only briefly.

f.g: Means “worm” or crimson dye; also the name of an Issachar clan.

n: Tola judged for twenty-three years — apparently a time of stability after civil war.

f.g: Led and governed, not only in battle.

n: Jair from Gilead, east of the Jordan, judges next for twenty-two years.
His thirty sons each rode a donkey and ruled a town — signs of wealth and status. The towns were called “villages of Jair.”

f.g: Young donkeys, ridden by people of rank.

n: Jair dies and is buried in Camon.
Israel’s idolatry reaches a new low: they serve the gods of seven nations and abandon the Lord completely.

f.w: forsook the LORD, and served not him
f.g: Not just adding gods, but dropping the Lord entirely.

n: God hands them over to two enemies at once: the Philistines in the west and the Ammonites in the east.

f.g: Descendants of Lot, living east of the Jordan.

n: For eighteen years Ammon crushed the Israelites in Gilead, east of the Jordan.
Ammon even crossed the Jordan to attack Judah, Benjamin, and Ephraim.
Israel cries out and, for once, openly confesses: we have sinned by forsaking God and serving Baals.
God answers by reviewing His record: I rescued you from Egypt, the Amorites, the Ammonites, the Philistines.
Also from Sidon, Amalek, and Maon — each time you cried, I saved you.

f.g: Possibly Midianites (as in the Greek Septuagint).

n: Yet you keep abandoning me, so I will save you no more. God’s patience is not to be taken for granted.

f.w: I will deliver you no more
f.g: A sharp warning meant to bring real repentance, not cheap requests.

n: With divine sarcasm, God says: go ask your chosen gods to save you. False gods cannot help in trouble.

f.w: Go and cry unto the gods which ye have chosen

n: Israel surrenders completely: do with us as you see fit, but please save us today. This is real repentance — submission, not bargaining.

f.w: do thou unto us whatsoever seemeth good unto thee

n: They act: they throw out their foreign gods and serve the Lord. And God could bear Israel’s misery no longer — a tender glimpse of His compassion.

f.w: his soul was grieved for the misery of Israel

n: Ammon gathers in Gilead; Israel gathers at Mizpeh in Gilead. The stage is set for battle.

f.g: A Mizpah in Gilead, east of the Jordan.

n: Gilead’s leaders have no champion and offer leadership to anyone who will start the fight — setting up Jephthah’s story.
